PSA: Beer Then Liquor, never sicker explained

New Year's Eve 1986, Arlington, TX. Not yet old enough to buy alcohol and not quite old enough to be friends with anyone old enough to buy alcohol, I had to settle for what I could get my hands on. That happened to be a case of Schlitz and a bottle of Cutty Sark. My best friend and I loaded the booze into the back of my Daytona, picked up our dates, and proceeded to party hop around north Arlington and HEB. We started off with the Schlitz because we didn't want to get too fucked up before midnight. At the last party we went to, we broke out the Cutty Sark and started slamming shots. Everything gets a little fuzzy after that, but I do remember desperately needing to go out on the balcony for some air where I threw up all over some guy's brand new suede shoes. I don't remember doing it, but I do remember him yelling about how I threw up all over his brand new suede shoes. I know there was fighting because I remember it ended when someone went over the balcony rail and everyone freaked out. I assume we won since David liked to fight as much as I did, but we both thought the other was the one who threw the guy off the balcony.. Our dates disappeared sometime between the shots and the dighting, and I'm pretty sure we never saw either of them again. That was the first time I ever heard the saying "beer before liquor, never sicker." It might have been more handy before the fact, but such is life.
